title: Chatterbox-Flash: Prior-Calibrated Block Diffusion for Streaming Zero-Shot TTS
claim: Resemble AI's arXiv paper in the Chatterbox line: AR decoder fine-tuned into block-diffusion for streaming zero-shot TTS; "high-fidelity synthesis comparable to strong autoregressive and non-autoregressive baselines"; the original Chatterbox (0.5B, MIT, 5-20 s reference, PerTh watermark on every output) has no paper
not_covered: Model description only; training data undisclosed (LibriSpeech overlap possible); PerTh watermark is a CLONE/STOCK-only systematic difference; no listener or audio-LLM behaviour study

title: F5-TTS: A Fairytaler that Fakes Fluent and Faithful Speech with Flow Matching
claim: Non-autoregressive flow-matching DiT TTS with filler-token text padding and Sway Sampling; RTF 0.15; 100K h public data; natural expressive zero-shot cloning; its LibriSpeech-PC WER/SIM protocol is the field standard
not_covered: Alternative clone engine; no downstream behavioural measurement

title: XTTS: a Massively Multilingual Zero-Shot Text-to-Speech Model
claim: Tortoise-based public zero-shot multilingual cloning system, 16 languages, SOTA in most
not_covered: Engine only; candidate second engine for engine-generality check

title: CosyVoice 2: Scalable Streaming Speech Synthesis with Large Language Models
claim: FSQ supervised speech tokens, pre-trained LLM backbone, chunk-aware causal flow matching; claims human-parity naturalness and virtually lossless streaming quality
not_covered: Parity claimed on MOS/SIM only; nothing on how a downstream model treats the output

title: Neural Codec Language Models are Zero-Shot Text to Speech Synthesizers
claim: VALL-E: TTS as LM over EnCodec tokens, 60K h, 3-second in-context cloning; outperforms prior zero-shot TTS on naturalness and speaker similarity; preserves prompt emotion and environment
not_covered: Origin of codec-token cloning (why RESYNTH control exists); no behavioural study

title: Seed-TTS: A Family of High-Quality Versatile Speech Generation Models
claim: AR and DiT TTS "virtually indistinguishable from human speech"; speaker similarity and naturalness match ground-truth human speech objectively and subjectively; reference/target zero-shot protocol on LibriSpeech test-clean
not_covered: Instrument reaches perceptual parity; no measurement of machine treatment of its output

title: WavLM: Large-Scale Self-Supervised Pre-Training for Full Stack Speech Processing
claim: Masked prediction + denoising SSL on 94k h; SOTA on SUPERB incl. speaker verification; WavLM-SV cosine is the standard TTS speaker-similarity (SIM) metric
not_covered: SIM measures identity retention, not provenance; a precondition for our arms, not a result

title: UTMOS: UTokyo-SaruLab System for VoiceMOS Challenge 2022
claim: SSL-fine-tuned ensemble MOS predictor, top on VoiceMOS 2022 main and OOD tracks; standard automatic naturalness score
not_covered: Predicts human naturalness ratings; scale uncalibrated on 2026 clones; within-study arm comparison only

title: DNSMOS P.835: A Non-Intrusive Perceptual Objective Speech Quality Metric to Evaluate Noise Suppressors
claim: Non-intrusive SIG/BAK/OVRL predictor, PCC 0.94/0.98/0.98 with P.835 human ratings
not_covered: Built for noise suppressors, not synthetic speech; quality covariate only

title: Codec-SUPERB: An In-Depth Analysis of Sound Codec Models
claim: Benchmark of neural codecs on content, paralinguistics, speaker and audio tasks plus signal metrics; codecs lose different information classes
not_covered: Downstream classifier loss, not generative audio-LLM behaviour toward resynthesised speech

title: High Fidelity Neural Audio Compression
claim: EnCodec: streaming encoder-decoder, multiscale spectrogram adversary, loss balancer; MUSHRA-superior at 24 kHz mono and 48 kHz stereo; the codec used for our RESYNTH arm
not_covered: No study of listener or model treatment of re-encoded vs original speech

title: High-Fidelity Audio Compression with Improved RVQGAN
claim: DAC: ~90x compression of 44.1 kHz audio at 8 kbps, universal single model, outperforms competing codecs, open weights
not_covered: Alternative control codec; same gap as EnCodec

title: CodecFake: Enhancing Anti-Spoofing Models Against Deepfake Audios from Codec-Based Speech Synthesis Systems
claim: First codec-based deepfake dataset; anti-spoofing models trained on standard data cannot detect codec-resynthesised speech until trained on CodecFake
not_covered: Shows resynthesis is a distinct detectable artefact class (motivates RESYNTH); dedicated detectors only, no audio LLM, no behavioural outcome

title: Human Perception of Audio Deepfakes
claim: 472 users, 14,912 rounds vs SOTA detector: humans and detectors share strengths and weaknesses; native speakers better, older participants worse, IT professionals no advantage
not_covered: Human explicit detection only; nothing on trust/grading or on audio LLMs

title: Warning: Humans cannot reliably detect speech deepfakes
claim: n=529 English and Mandarin listeners spot deepfakes 73% of the time; no language difference; example-based training helps only slightly
not_covered: Human, explicit, 2023 synthesis; supplies the D4 comparison point, no implicit behavioural measure

title: ASVspoof 5: Design Collection and Validation of Resources for Spoofing Deepfake and Adversarial Attack Detection Using Crowdsourced Speech
claim: Crowdsourced ~2,000-speaker database, 32 TTS/VC/adversarial attack algorithms optimised against surrogate detectors, speaker-disjoint protocols
not_covered: Dedicated detector evaluation; no generalist audio-LLM, no matched behavioural outcome

title: PhonemeDF: A Synthetic Speech Dataset for Audio Deepfake Detection and Naturalness Evaluation
claim: Parallel real (LibriSpeech subset) and synthetic speech from 4 TTS + 3 VC systems, phoneme-aligned; real-vs-synthetic phoneme KLD predicts detector performance
not_covered: Closest stimulus construction to ours but outcome is detector accuracy and phoneme fidelity, not audio-LLM behaviour

title: Choice of Voices: A Large-Scale Evaluation of Text-to-Speech Voice Quality for Long-Form Content
claim: CHI 2020; 18 TTS voices, 3 human voices, text control, ~1,090 crowd raters on listening experience, clarity/quality, comprehension: "TTS voices are close to rivaling human voices, yet no single voice outperforms the others"
not_covered: Human raters, unmatched speakers, stock TTS not clones; comprehension in listener not model

title: The Human Takes It All: Humanlike Synthesized Voices Are Perceived as Less Eerie and More Likable
claim: 95 adults rate IBM Watson, robot Sophia and human voices; human-likeness predicts lower eeriness and higher likability; paralinguistic cues used to separate human from artificial
not_covered: Human listeners, no same-speaker clone condition, no machine listener

title: Robot Voices in Daily Life: Vocal Human-Likeness and Application Context as Determinants of User Acceptance
claim: 165 participants, five voices at graded realism; anthropomorphism, eeriness and acceptance vary with realism and application domain
not_covered: Human judges only; supplies context-dependent trust framing for ASSIST outcome

title: Persuasive Synthetic Speech: Voice Perception and User Behaviour
claim: CUI 2020; debating-style synthetic voice rated significantly more truthful and involved than audiobook-style synthetic voice in a flight-booking agent task, but recommendation-following unchanged
not_covered: Compares two synthetic voices, not synthetic vs real; behaviour measured in the human

title: Speech synthesis technologies for individuals with vocal disabilities: Voice banking and reconstruction
claim: Overview of clinical speech synthesis and the Edinburgh voice banking project for MND/ALS and Parkinson's: personalised synthetic voices for AAC from pre-loss recordings
not_covered: HMM era; no study of third-party or machine response to a banked voice

title: Voice banking for people living with motor neurone disease: Views and expectations
claim: >80% of plwMND develop speech difficulties, most use AAC; generic synthesized voices seen as impersonal and a barrier to AAC acceptance; voice banking argued to preserve identity
not_covered: Clinical/qualitative; nothing on whether voice agents treat a banked voice differently

title: An Evaluation Framework for Text-to-Speech Voice Reconstruction
claim: 17 zero-shot TTS systems, 193 speakers with speech disorders; MOS insufficient; BWS with situational framing plus dual-reference distributional intelligibility/identity measure
not_covered: Evaluates reconstruction for people, not machine treatment of reconstructed voices

title: EVA-Bench: A New End-to-end Framework for Evaluating Voice Agents
claim: Bot-to-bot audio conversations with TTS-voiced simulated users; 213 scenarios, 12 systems, accent/noise perturbation suite (mean delta up to 0.314)
not_covered: Every caller is synthetic and treated as inert; provenance is not a perturbation axis

title: VAmoS Bench: Voice Agent Simulation Bench
claim: End-to-end containment benchmark; simulated caller reaches a credit-card support agent over audio, 100 scenarios, one-third adversarial, SQL tool-call grading
not_covered: Synthetic caller voice assumed inert; no real-vs-synthetic comparison

title: Librispeech: An ASR corpus based on public domain audio books
claim: ~1000 h 16 kHz read English from LibriVox public-domain audiobooks; test-clean is the speaker-disjoint clean eval split; licence CC BY 4.0 (openslr.org/12, read live)
not_covered: Built for ASR; test-clean doubles as the standard zero-shot TTS eval set so our stimuli sit where cloning papers report numbers

title: LibriTTS: A Corpus Derived from LibriSpeech for Text-to-Speech
claim: 585 h at 24 kHz from 2,456 LibriSpeech speakers re-cut for TTS; neural TTS trained on it reaches >4.0 naturalness MOS
not_covered: Documents that LibriSpeech speakers are common TTS training data: possible seen-speaker contamination for CLONE; Chatterbox training data undisclosed
